title: How Africa Can Leverage the US-China Thaw
content: As dollar borrowing costs soar, Chinese rates are approaching record lows. This divergence, combined with the US-China thaw, creates an opportunity for African governments: partner with the US on gas and with China on solar and storage, and tap lower-cost Asian capital markets to finance investments in both.

title: Closing NATO’s Deterrence Gap

India will return to the negotiating table only after Pakistan dismantles, comprehensively and verifiably, its state-supported terrorist networks.

title: The Next Era of Reform Must Be About Capability
content: Economic development should no longer be measured solely by how much finance is mobilized or how much fiscal space is created. It must also be judged by whether countries emerge more capable of setting their own priorities, responding to challenges, and seizing new opportunities to shape their own future.

If serving the public interest is the goal, everyone relying on the technology's output has a duty to provide high-quality input.

title: Brazil’s Voters Have Moved

The Brazilian electorate is older, more devout, and more preoccupied with crime and personal security than it once was.

title: Does Inclusive Finance Really Need Stablecoins?
content: Today, 1.3 billion adults—more than half of them women—remain excluded from the formal financial system, and lower-income consumers still struggle to find and access the financial products and services they need. Contrary to much hype, stablecoins are not the best way to solve either of these problems.

content: America and Israel's unilateral aggression against Iran lacked international legitimacy and predictably destabilized the entire region. title: Is Russia’s Placement on the Security Council Legal?

content: To help Nepal move from rescue and relief toward reconstruction, money-transfer companies and banks ought to waive fees on remittances sent to the country for at least two months. Doing so could provide additional relief totaling several times more than what a recent emergency appeal by the United Nations generated.

content: In recent years, the OECD has strayed from its core mission of coordinating economic policy among the US and its allies, instead building programs around gender budgeting and environmental justice. The Trump administration should use its leverage at the organization to return its focus to economics and national security.
